findings.evidence: scripts/rollout_project.py: `item[1].group(1).strip("'\"") != DEFAULT_RUNNER` treats a quoted value as the default. docs/managed-rollout.md says all-`ubuntu-latest` projects need "no new step". tests/test_ci_runner_selection.py `test_rollout_treats_a_quoted_default_runner_as_the_default` asserts only `rollout_outcome == "default"` and never runs `copier update`. A file with quoted `runs-on` differs from the baseline render, so Copier may leave a `.rej` or `platform_doctor` may report a mismatch. That would be the failure the preflight exists to prevent.
findings.summary: A quoted `"ubuntu-latest"` or `'ubuntu-latest'` runner is classified as `default`. The docs promise the ordinary update then runs with no new step. The test checks only the preflight outcome, not the update that follows.

findings.evidence: scripts/rollout_project.py `platform_doctor_module()` loads `PLATFORM_ROOT/template/scripts/platform_doctor.py`. `migrate_ci_runner_answers` reads the target's `copier.yml` via `git show {version}:copier.yml` but takes the doctor from the working tree. The docstring says it applies "the exact runner-label rule CI will enforce".
findings.summary: The rollout applies the runner-label rule from the platform checkout's working-tree `platform_doctor.py`. It does not use the doctor shipped in the target tag. The two can drift, so the migrated answers may be judged by a rule different from the one CI later enforces.
